videos.title: Agentforce Long-Horizon Agents
videos.focus: Planning and supervising work that continues across sessions
videos.summary: Salesforce explains why long-horizon agents need measurable goals, plans, tools, context, guardrails, memory and durable execution. The demonstration shows a seller reviewing an evolving plan and approving actions over time. It is a product lesson, so architecture and benefit claims remain first-party rather than independent performance evidence.
videos.why_it_matters: Use the lesson to turn a vague autonomous goal into a measurable outcome, approved tool set, review cadence and stop condition before any agent works across multiple sessions.

verification.content_review_basis: Reviewed the complete English caption transcript, exact Vidyard identity and 237.208-second runtime.

playback_evidence.method: Fresh signed-out Chrome session opened the exact public Vidyard player and activated its visible play control.
playback_evidence.result: Observed duration 237.208 seconds with readyState 4, paused false and currentTime advancing beyond 5.55 seconds.

quality_review.learning_objective: Translate a long-running business goal into measurable scope, a reviewable plan, explicit tools, permission boundaries and a human steering cadence.
quality_review.practical_action: Choose one recurring goal, define its success measure, allowed tools, approval points, progress update cadence and stop condition.
quality_review.selected_over_alternatives: Selected because the exact publisher player advanced signed out, the complete captions support an instructional lesson and the goal-and-plan method differs from the administration video.

content_evidence.scope: Reviewed the complete caption file from immediate-task limitations through goal definition, planning, memory, durable execution, approval, adaptation and closing caveats.

quality_review.promotional_assessment: Salesforce demonstrates its own product, so the transferable planning method is retained while product capability claims remain publisher assertions.
transferable_takeaways: Define a measurable, time-bound goal before allowing an agent to begin multi-session work.
List tools, context and approval boundaries in the initial plan and review revisions before activation.
Require progress updates and a stop condition so adaptation remains visible and reversible.

videos.title: From a Workday Expert: Self-Service Agent
videos.focus: Configuring and testing a noncoding employee self-service agent
videos.summary: Workday Education demonstrates registering a Self-Service Agent, enabling Skills and tools, configuring fallback guidance, checking domain security and testing access before deployment. The lesson also shows employee and manager use cases. It reflects Workday’s product and automation claims, so teams should validate outcomes and permissions in a nonproduction environment.
videos.why_it_matters: Use the procedure to create a configuration checklist: confirm required security policies, register the agent, enable only needed capabilities, define fallback behavior and test each user group before release.

quality_review.learning_objective: Configure a self-service agent through registration, limited capabilities, fallback handling, security verification and user-specific testing before production release.
quality_review.practical_action: Create a five-step checklist covering registration, capability scope, fallback, domain security and test evidence for each intended user group.
